description:
Elixir warns 'variable "x" is unused (if the variable is not meant to be used, prefix it with an underscore)' for every binding that is never read: function parameters, pattern bindings in case/fn/receive heads, and match bindings. fz has no such diagnostic: src/diag/codes.rs has no unused-variable code, and grep for 'unused' in src finds no warning (checked at develop f822f0f84).

Why now: while writing up the specialization policy, a parameter the body never uses (sink(_x) and sink(x) alike) turned out to be something keying could be asked to optimize away. It is a mistake in the program and the author should hear about it; keying should not treat it specially.

Acceptance:
- def f(x), do: 1 warns once at x with a new code (lint-style, e.g. variable/unused), with Elixir's wording.
- def f(_x), do: 1 and def f(_), do: 1 do not warn.
- A variable used only in a guard, a pin (^x), or a nested fn counts as used.
- Each clause is judged on its own, as Elixir does.
- Fixtures: one oracle-free warning fixture per case above; the existing suite shows no new warnings (any that appear are real and fixed in lib/ or the fixtures, named in the commit).
- Docs: the guide's diagnostics list names the code.
title: A variable that is bound and never used warns, unless its name starts with an underscore
